historicalReferences: Think back to 1966, when Ken Miles and Lloyd Ruby famously won the 24 Hours of Daytona, only to be controversially demoted.
The 1959 Daytona 500 saw Lee Petty narrowly beat Johnny Beauchamp in a photo finish, a moment etched in racing lore.
Remember 1979? The Daytona 500 finish where Cale Yarborough and Donnie Allison crashed, leading to a fistfight on the infield!
The incredible endurance of the 24 Hours of Daytona has produced countless stories of triumph and heartbreak over the years.
Daytona's high banks have always been a proving ground for drivers and engineers alike, pushing technology to its very limits.
The sheer speeds achieved on this oval have made Daytona a magnet for record attempts and daredevil feats.
Many a championship campaign has been decided right here at Daytona, with fortunes won and lost in the blink of an eye.
The names of Andretti, Earnhardt, and Petty are synonymous with Daytona, their legacies forever intertwined with this iconic track.
Let's not forget the stories of the underdogs, the privateer teams who came to Daytona and defied the odds.
The roar of the engines here echoes through the decades, a reminder of Daytona's enduring appeal.
cornerCallouts: They're hurtling towards turn one now, the West Banking, a critical corner for setting up the run down the back straight.

The drivers are really pushing hard through the Bus Stop, trying to gain every tenth of a second.
Heading into the East Banking, you can really see the cars fighting for grip here as they accelerate out.
They're approaching the finish line now, after the final turn, a crucial moment to maximize speed.
strategyPoints: Tire degradation will be a major factor today on this abrasive Daytona surface, particularly through the infield section.
With the length of the Historic layout, fuel consumption will be a key consideration. Teams will need to balance speed with efficiency.
The pit window here is relatively short, meaning the timing of the stops will be absolutely crucial. A slight delay could be costly.
Running in clean air will be a significant advantage, allowing drivers to manage their tires and fuel more effectively.
The draft will play a huge role on the oval sections, so expect to see plenty of strategic positioning and close racing.
Undercut or overcut? Teams will be constantly analyzing the data to determine the optimal pit stop strategy.
Safety car periods can dramatically alter the race, so teams will need to be prepared to react quickly to any unexpected incidents.
The setup of the car is a delicate balance between speed on the oval and handling in the infield. Finding the sweet spot will be key.
weatherCommentary: The Florida heat is relentless today, putting immense strain on the drivers and their equipment.
Humidity is high here at Daytona, making it even more challenging for the drivers in the cockpit.
There's a chance of thunderstorms later this afternoon, which could throw a real curveball into the race strategy.
The wind is picking up, which could affect the car's stability on the high-speed sections.
The track temperature is soaring, which will further exacerbate tire degradation.
